newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: CRICKET-SRI LANKAN SPINNERS ENGINEER ZIMBABWE COLLAPSE.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-SRI LANKAN SPINNERS ENGINEER ZIMBABWE COLLAPSE.

text.p: Sri Lanka spinners Muthiah Muralitharan and Jayantha Silva captured four wickets apiece on Wednesday as Zimbabwe collapsed to 141 all out at tea on the first day of the second test.
Sri Lanka were 86 for three in reply before a third stoppage for rain forced the players to leave the field for the day with 13 of the scheduled 90 overs remaining.
Zimbabwe, beaten by an innings in the first test, were handily placed at 119 for two before off-spinner Muralitharan and left-armer Silva engineered a stunning collapse.

Zimbabwe captain Alistair Campbell, who had elected to bat on another bare pitch after winning the toss at the Sinhalese Sports Club, started the slide with an irresponsible shot after adding 65 for the third wicket with opener Grant Flower.
Campbell jumped out to drive spinner Silva, missed the ball and was stumped by Romesh Kaluwitharana metres down the pitch after scoring 36.

Flower's innings of 52, which included six fours in nearly three hours of solid defence, was ended by Muralitharan who had him caught at slip as the innings folded within an hour of Campbell's dismissal.
Muralitharan finished with four for 40 off 20 overs and Silva four for 16 from 10.1 overs.

Zimbabwe leg-spinner Paul Strang struck back when Sri Lanka batted, finishing the day with figures of 7-3-8-2 after picking up the prize scalps of Sanath Jayasuriya for a rapidly struck 41 off 46 balls with a six and six fours plus Aravinda de Silva for 16.

Paul's younger brother Bryan Strang, who took the place of Heath Streak when he failed to pass a fitness test on an injured groin, claimed the other wicket, dismissing opener Roshan Mahanama for three.
